clue.text: Good day ruined for one MP tonight

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician's pleasant day is spoilt by what happens tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals an anagram of FORONEMPTONIGHT, giving the old Irish-flavoured greeting. The held text had a stray 'to' that the printed page lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheery, old-fashioned greeting used in the morning, equivalent to wishing someone a good day.

clue.text: Soldier monarch originally raised in rank

indicators.note: the monarch and the first letter are placed in the middle of the word for rank

parts.note: a rank or row is a tier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word raised

explanation.surface: A soldier who has risen through the ranks because of royal favour.
explanation.walkthrough: A TERRIER is a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrier is informal British slang for a member of the Territorial Army reserve.

clue.text: Indicate how to repair masonry

definitions.meaning: to indicate is to show with a finger, to direct attention
renewing the mortar between bricks is a building task named by the same verb

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to direct attention by gesture and to refill the mortar joints of brickwork.

clue.text: Female's unpleasant quality, being outspoken

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
rankness is the quality of being foul or offensive

explanation.surface: A woman's disagreeable trait is that she speaks her mind too freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outspoken is candour, plain speaking without reserve.

clue.text: Stuffing for certain seats

parts.note: old upholstered sofas were padded with what grows on a horse's mane and tail

explanation.definitionFit: Horse-derived padding was the traditional filling packed into upholstered sofas and settees.

clue.text: Reportedly occupied a position in Asian city

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is said aloud to give the city

parts.note: manned a lay: to man is to occupy a post, and a lay is a position or arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone took up a post in an Asian city, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lay' is a position, as in 'the lay of the land'; MANNED A LAY sounds like the city in Myanmar (Burma).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the second city of Myanmar, the former royal capital of Burma.

clue.text: Cancel brief

definitions.meaning: to cancel a debt or penalty is to waive it
a brief is the scope of a task or responsibility

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to waive a debt or penalty; as a noun it is the terms of reference given to someone.

clue.text: Charge men to install a flashing light

indicators.note: to install is to put something inside, so the article goes inside the word for charge

parts.note: to charge someone formally with a crime is to indict them
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for men in the army

explanation.surface: Someone is charging workmen to fit a blinking lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's flashing light that signals a turn is called this, a winker or blinker.

clue.text: Coward and convict hauled up in sailing vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauling up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Noel Coward was the English playwright and wit
a lag is slang for a prisoner, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A timid person and a prisoner were dragged up aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is not a frightened person but Noel Coward; NOEL LAG reversed gives GAL LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing ship of the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: In financial disaster contemplating lost millions

indicators.note: lost means a piece goes missing from the word for contemplating

parts.note: rumination is deep thought or contemplation
M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: Someone in a financial crisis is pondering how millions went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost millions' removes the M from RUMINATION. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is complete ruin, here the collapse of one's finances.

clue.text: Metre associated with line at end of poem, for example

indicators.note: at end of places the line abbreviation after the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poetic metre goes with a final line of verse, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the definition is 'example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is an example to follow, a pattern worth copying.

clue.text: New pupils —— vague number — captured in single photograph

indicators.note: captured in means held inside the single-plus-photograph pair

parts.note: I, the Roman one, stands for single
a take is a single shot in photography or filming
N stands for an indefinite number, as in the nth time

explanation.surface: A new class of schoolchildren of uncertain size was caught in one class picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's intake is the batch of new pupils it admits in a given year.

clue.text: Completed single revolutionary work of art

parts.note: completed means over and done, past
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A lone rebel finished a piece of artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is an artistic work imitating the style of another artist or period.

clue.text: Encircling us, wild herd stampeded

indicators.note: the scrambled herd surrounds the word us
wild suggests the letters of herd running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild herd of cattle stampeded around us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes RHED from HERD, which encircles US.
explanation.definitionFit: To stampede is to charge headlong, the same as to have rushed.

clue.text: Killer fish found in rivers, lurking under stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, lurking under puts the rest below the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the letters for rivers

parts.note: R is river, doubled for the plural
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A deadly fish dwells in rivers, hiding beneath rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun but is the verb ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles the victim.

clue.text: Influential Russian, for example, appointed by leader of revolution

indicators.note: leader of points to the opening letter of revolution

parts.note: as can mean for example, such as
put in means installed or appointed

explanation.surface: An influential Russian, say, was installed by the head of a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTIN in the wordplay looks like another Russian but here is just PUT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the mystic who held great sway over the last Tsar's family.

clue.text: Distraught chap rings one doctor up … using this?

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the jumbled letters surround the word one
distraught suggests letters thrown into disorder
in a down clue, up means reading the doctor abbreviation from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An upset man calls a doctor from a public booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distraught' rearranges CHAP to PHCA, which rings ONE; 'up' turns DR into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepaid card used in a public payphone, so the definition asks what the caller is using.

clue.text: Story about the Italian Mafia leader is what The Godfather turned out to be

definitions.text: what The Godfather turned out to be

indicators.note: about means surrounding the Italian article and the initial

parts.note: a fable is a short story with a moral
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of Mafia

explanation.surface: A Mafia tale became a successful film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia novel proved suitable for making into a film, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Writer wants money principally from this crime novel

indicators.note: novel suggests a new arrangement of the letters of this crime
principally points to the first letter of money

explanation.surface: A crime novelist wants this book to be a money-spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants money principally from' takes M out of THIS CRIME; 'novel' then rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie is the famous English crime writer.

clue.text: Crew member having care of religious group

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
pi is slang for pious or religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A crew member looks after a faith community.
explanation.definitionFit: A copilot is the second pilot in an aircraft's flight crew.

clue.text: Puts up panels

definitions.meaning: to board someone is to give them lodging, putting them up

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means lodges a guest; as a plural noun it means flat pieces of timber.

clue.text: Singular display of heroism, eliminating a source of evil

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: eliminating means the letter a is removed from the word for heroism

parts.note: courage is bravery shown in action

explanation.surface: A unique heroic act wipes out a source of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering, a plague or source of affliction.

clue.text: Current affairs programme showing soldiers invading foreign land

indicators.note: invading means the soldiers go inside the country's name

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America
OR, other ranks, means soldiers

explanation.surface: A TV news show shows troops invading another country.
explanation.walkthrough: PANORAMA is the long-running BBC current affairs programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's flagship investigative documentary series has this title.

clue.text: Park in front of church for a look round

indicators.note: in front of places the park word before the church abbreviation

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone walks round the park beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link; a REC is the British name for a local recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting look round.

clue.text: Two ducks trailing behind male bird

indicators.note: trailing behind puts the ducks after the male

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two of them are a pair of O's

explanation.surface: A pair of ducks follows a drake.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin, a flightless bird.

clue.text: Served up wafer-thin slice that isn't kosher food

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read upwards
a slice is a part cut from the middle of the hyphenated words

explanation.surface: A thin wafer is served that breaks Jewish dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: AFERT from the middle of 'wafer-thin', read upwards, gives TREFA.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefa is food forbidden under Jewish dietary laws, the opposite of kosher.

clue.text: Seal promotion

definitions.meaning: a seal is a stopper closing an opening
a promotional mention or puff for a product

explanation.definitionFit: A plug stops up a hole, and in advertising it is a favourable mention that publicises something.

clue.text: Drop by about one, turning a little purple

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembled word is turned round
about means the visit word goes around the one

parts.note: to drop by is to call on someone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone drops in around one o'clock and turns slightly purple.
explanation.walkthrough: CALL around I makes CALIL, which 'turning' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale shade of purple, only slightly purple.

clue.text: Singer, young chap, always finishes after "The Party's Over"

indicators.note: the young chap and always come at the end, after the curtailed party
over means finished, so the party loses its final letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
a lad is a young man
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A young singer keeps performing after the song about a party ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Party's Over' is a song title, but here it means BALL with its end cut off, BAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of ballads.

clue.text: Urged to join dance in old country event

indicators.note: in places the dance and urged inside the old country

parts.note: Thrace was an ancient region of the Balkans

indicators.note: to join means the urged word is attached after the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
egged on means urged

explanation.surface: Encouraged to join a dance in an ancient land's festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-legged race is a sports-day event where pairs run with adjacent legs tied together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic school sports-day or fete race event.
